transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

[Heading: High-voltage heating circuit fault]
I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Please stop immediately. Do not touch any internal components or attempt to test the magnetron yourself. Microwaves contain high-voltage capacitors that can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged, and working inside the casing without proper discharge equipment is extremely dangerous. The symptoms you describe (running normally but no heat) point to a failure in the high-voltage heating circuit—likely the magnetron, HV diode, capacitor, or transformer. Because this involves live high-voltage parts that are not safe for DIY repair, I strongly advise against proceeding with any internal checks. If your microwave is under warranty, contact Samsung support. Otherwise, you will need a qualified appliance engineer to safely diagnose and replace the faulty component. Please put the cover back on (or leave it off if you're unsure) and keep the unit unplugged until help arrives.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
